title: Learning Flexible Time-windowed Granger Causality Integrating Heterogeneous Interventional Time Series Data

problem.claim: Infer causal structures from time series data while improving the clarity of Granger-causal structure identification.

gap.claim: Existing methods have not addressed imperfect interventions with unknown targets, and identifiability remains unresolved for Granger causality with unknown intervention targets in complex network models.

contributions.claim: A theoretically grounded method infers Granger causal structure and identifies unknown intervention targets using heterogeneous interventional time series data.
Learning Granger causal structure and recovering intervention targets can mutually promote each other.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Comparative experiments report that the method outperforms several robust baseline methods for learning Granger causal structure from interventional time series data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Granger causality is used broadly for inferring causal structures from time series because of its explainability and compatibility with deep neural network prediction models.
Interventional data is used to help decipher causal structures more unambiguously.
Imperfect interventions with unknown targets and related identifiability issues in complex networks remain insufficiently addressed.
The work introduces a theoretically grounded method using heterogeneous interventional time series data to infer causal structure and recover unknown targets.
Comparative experiments report better performance than several robust baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly learns Granger causal structure and recovers unknown intervention targets from heterogeneous interventional time series data.

interpretation.claim: Estimating causal structure and intervention targets may provide mutually informative signals.

application.claim: When intervention targets are unknown, combine heterogeneous interventional time series with joint structure and target learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the assumptions or conditions under which the mutual promotion or identifiability result holds.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the method's algorithmic details or theoretical assumptions.
The datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline configurations, and numerical results are not provided.
The abstract does not describe the intervention model, network settings, or limitations.
